message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering public vulnerability information newly reported or materially updated in the last 24 hours for the scheduled July 19, 2026 IST run. Confirmed relevant findings were found for WordPress, Ubuntu, and OpenSSL.

**Finding 1: WordPress 7.0.2 security release**

- Product: WordPress
- Issue: CVE-2026-60137 / GHSA-fpp7-x2x2-2mjf and CVE-2026-63030 / GHSA-ff9f-jf42-662q
- Severity: WordPress describes the release as addressing one critical and one high severity security issue.
- Description: WordPress released version 7.0.2 to fix a facilitated SQL injection issue and a REST API batch-route confusion plus SQL injection issue that can lead to remote code execution.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes WordPress, and the official WordPress security release explicitly names affected WordPress branches and fixed backport releases.
- Source: WordPress.org release notice: https://wordpress.org/news/2026/07/wordpress-7-0-2-release/

**Finding 2: Ubuntu Linux kernel security updates**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: USN-8490-1 and USN-8490-2, covering multiple Linux kernel CVEs including CVE-2026-43304, CVE-2026-43341, CVE-2026-43376, CVE-2026-31659, CVE-2026-31669, and many others.
- Severity: Not stated as a single overall severity by Canonical.
- Description: Canonical published kernel updates for Ubuntu 25.10 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, including real-time kernel packages, fixing numerous kernel issues across networking, filesystems, USB over IP, cryptographic API, NFS, SMB, IPv6, Netfilter, and other subsystems.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and the notices explicitly apply to maintained Ubuntu releases and official Ubuntu kernel packages.
- Source: Canonical USN-8490-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8490-1 ; Canonical USN-8490-2: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8490-2

**Finding 3: OpenSSL HollowByte denial-of-service issue**

- Product: OpenSSL
- Issue: HollowByte memory exhaustion issue; no CVE assigned as of the reviewed sources.
- Severity: Not clearly stated; OpenSSL reportedly treated the change as hardening rather than a CVE security advisory.
- Description: Okta Red Team disclosed a denial-of-service issue where a remote unauthenticated attacker can use a very small malicious TLS payload to force disproportionate server-side memory allocation before the TLS handshake completes. Okta reports fixes were included in OpenSSL 4.0.1 and backported to 3.6.3, 3.5.7, 3.4.6, and 3.0.21.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes OpenSSL, and this issue affects OpenSSL server-side TLS handling according to Okta's technical write-up.
- Source: Okta Security: https://sec.okta.com/articles/2026/06/openssl-hollowbtye-a-dos-hiding-in-11-bytes/ ; secondary confirmation: Security Affairs: https://securityaffairs.com/195588/hacking/openssl-fixes-hollowbyte-memory-exhaustion-bug.html

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for WordPress deployments because the vendor describes one issue as critical and enabled forced auto-updates for affected sites. Ubuntu kernel updates should be handled through the standard OS patch cycle with reboot planning. OpenSSL/HollowByte should be reviewed for internet-facing TLS services even though no CVE or official OpenSSL security advisory was identified.
